annotation.title_clean: India AI Governance Guidelines: Enabling Safe and Trusted AI Innovation
annotation.title_en: India AI Governance Guidelines: Enabling Safe and Trusted AI Innovation
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India (Drafting Committee; published via PIB)
annotation.venue: Press Information Bureau, Government of India
annotation.summary_en: India's national AI governance guidelines from MeitY, setting seven sutras and recommendations across infrastructure, capacity building, regulation, risk mitigation, accountability and institutions. It favours innovation over restraint, relying on existing laws, voluntary measures and techno-legal tools, with new bodies (AIGG, AI Safety Institute) and an action plan.
key_provisions_or_claims: Seven sutras: Trust, People First, Innovation over Restraint, Fairness & Equity, Accountability, Understandable by Design, Safety/Resilience/Sustainability.
Existing laws largely suffice; no standalone AI law now, with targeted amendments as needed.
Creates AI Governance Group, Technology & Policy Expert Committee, and AI Safety Institute.
Recommends India-specific risk classification framework and AI incident reporting database.
Promotes voluntary frameworks, human-in-the-loop oversight in critical sectors, and techno-legal measures.
